key_evidence_accepted: The entire story about the abduction by car and the forced marriage was seemingly concocted. Even after the alleged marriage with A-1, PW-2 continued to be a willing partner in the entire episode. She did not protest nor made any complaint though she had the opportunity to do so on many occasions. The conduct of PW-2 from the time of her alleged abduction till the time of her alleged recovery was not natural for a girl who had been compelled to marry and subjected to illicit sexual intercourse.
witness_credibility: The testimony of PW-2 does not satisfy the test of being free from basic infirmities or improbabilities. The conduct of PW-2 and the inconsistencies in her testimony, along with the father's lack of involvement and the absence of reliable evidence regarding the transfer certificate, cast doubt on the credibility of the main witnesses.
post_offence_conduct: PW-2 did not make any complaint on so many occasions when she had the opportunity to do so. She did not raise any protest or complain to anyone at any of the stages after being allegedly abducted. She did not make any complaint at the residence of Selvi, sister of A-1, or when she was taken to the house of PW5 or to the police station.
trial_duration: Charge-sheet filed against A-1 for offences punishable under Sections 366 and 376 IPC and accused Nos. 2 to 8 for offences punishable under Sections 366 and 376 read with Section 109 IPC. The trial court convicted all the accused. The conviction was affirmed by the High Court.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not specified
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed against A-1 for offences punishable under Sections 366 and 376 IPC and accused Nos. 2 to 8 for offences punishable under Sections 366 and 376 read with Section 109 IPC
procedural_irregularity: The trial court as well as the High Court failed to take into consideration the inherent improbabilities in the case sought to be projected by the prosecution. The findings recorded by both the Courts below were perverse and unsupportable by the evidence on record.
appeal_history: The conviction of the accused-appellants was challenged on the ground that the conclusions reached by both the Courts below were perverse and that they ignored the inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of the witnesses. It was contended that the facts of the case clearly suggested that there was no question of any abduction, forcible marriage or rape. Per contra, the State contended that the prosecution version was consistent and further that, in exercise of its powers under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court normally does not interfere with the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below and, thus, the instant appeals were liable to be dismissed. Allowance of the appeals, the Court held: Even though the powers of this Court under Article 136 of the Constitution are very wide, but in criminal appeals, this Court would not interfere with the concurrent findings of facts, save in very exceptional cases.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution alleged that PW-2 was abducted, forcibly married, and raped by A-1, with PW-2 being a minor at the relevant date. The prosecution version was consistent and sought to implicate the accused in the alleged abduction, forced marriage, and rape.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the entire story of abduction and forced marriage was concocted. PW-2's father suspected she was romantically involved with A-1, and her disappearance was presumed to be his responsibility. The conduct of PW-2 was unnatural for a girl who had been compelled to marry and subjected to illicit sexual intercourse.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the assessment of evidence by the High Court is accepted as final unless the conclusions are manifestly perverse and unsupportable by the evidence on record. It also emphasized that corroboration is not a sine qua non for conviction in rape cases if the victim's testimony does not suffer from basic infirmities or improbabilities.
precedent_relied_upon: Birad Mal Singhvi v. Anand Purohit, 1988 (Suppl.) SCC 604; Narbada Devi Gupta v. Birendra Kumar Jaiswal, (2003) 8 SCC 745; Jaya Mala v. Home Secretary, Government of Jammu & Kashmir & Ors., (1982) 2 SCC 538; Ravinder Singh Gorkhi v. State of U.P., (2006) 5 SCC 584; Rameshwar v. State of Rajasthan, (1952) SCR 377
judicial_mitigating_factors: The conduct of PW-2, including her willingness to stay with A-1 after the alleged marriage and not making any complaints despite having opportunities to do so, was considered.
other_sentence_order: The accused-appellants were acquitted and directed to be released forthwith.
